[organamisms] People shitting on non stick and saying to get stainless steel - everything I've read says you need to have the pan hot and the food needs to be dry and room temp before adding otherwise it'll cool the pan and stick. I've tried in the past and that's seemed to be the case.
Don't you find limits to what you can do on stainless steel, E.g. scrambled eggs or fish which can't be blasted at high temps?
Genuine question, I haven't had luck the last time I tried with stainless steel!
[Shon] google PFAS carcinogen for why everyone is recommending stainless. Then look up the Leidenfrost effect for how to cook with SS, not super easy but worth your longevity.
[lovrekn] Every nonstick I’ve had can only do scrambled eggs for the first year or so, after that it’s sticking anyway
This means 1) the nonstick coating that you used to have is no longer helping your food to not stick, meaning it no longer has an edge over stainless steel and more worryingly 2) you have most likely ingested this coating
When I do my scrambled eggs on the stainless I just accept that a small layer will be sticking. It’s way way easier to clean than nonstick though because you can’t damage the surface, no matter how rough you are. Hot water, my metal scourer and 20 seconds is literally all I need.. put some elbow grease in and it’s good as new.
I cook delicate fish in the oven, not on the stainless. I cook Salmon on the stainless skin side down when I want a crispy skin, there’s heaps of videos on YouTube. Just search for crispy salmon stainless steel
[whichwhatwho] It's just the same histrionic response to RoundUp/glyphosate. If you inject the raw product into your brain, you might get cancer, rightfully so but for us mere mortals who just cook something at a normal frequency or spray weeds like a normal person, nothing happens.

[jimojr] Probably better to get the Wolstead Stonetek Classic Ceramic 6pc (other brands may advertise a similar set as 9pc) Cookware Set for $100 from Kitchen Warehouse . I bought a Wolstead Superior+ Non-Stick Induction Wok 32cm for $60 today. I was surprised by the packaging and the quality . I don’t know how long the non-stick coating will last, though.
[lovrekn] Woks are the one piece of cookware that are least suited to having a non stick surface. Woks need to be heated to a very high heat, nonstick surfaces arent allowed to be heated to high heat (even the manufacturers state they pose a health risk at these temperatures)
[jimojr] You mean in restaurants. For home cooking, you don't need to heat a wok that much. Keeping it below 200°C still cooks food perfectly well. Also, if you cook at restaurant style high heat, you'll end up cleaning the kitchen every week because of all the grease. That's why we switched to non-stick woks more than 20 years ago. Now I only need to clean the kitchen about once a month instead of every week.
[liongalahad] RRP when it comes to pans and knives is most of the times basically a legalized scam, with hyper inflated RRP that make the actual correct price look like a heavily discounted bargain.
[webmonkey] Baccarat stuff is trash, the pans somehow get warped and form a dip in the centre.
